result.title: TurnFlow: Benchmarking User-State Reasoning in Multi-Turn LLM Agents via Scene-Guided User Simulation
result.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through conversational interfaces, yet strong single-turn performance does not imply reliability in multi-turn settings. Multi-turn assistance requires a model to maintain an evolving representation of user requirements and to reason over it before complying with later requests. Failures can therefore be subtle: models may fail to recognize a changed constraint or hidden conflict, or recognize it without enforcing it in the final response. Existing benchmarks primarily test fully specified prompts, long-context recall, or controlled domain environments, leaving open-domain requirement reconciliation undermeasured. We introduce TurnFlow, an interactive benchmark for evaluating whether models preserve, revise, and act on user requirements across turns. TurnFlow combines adaptive user simulation with verifiable judging, allowing conversations to unfold naturally while keeping hidden requirements and pass/fail criteria controlled. In our evaluation, nine LLMs achieve overall pass rates from 42.86% to 59.59% on 490 scenarios. Performance varies substantially across challenge types: models perform well on Stateful Multi-Constraint Following but remain considerably less reliable on Scope Creep and Goal Shift. These results reveal persistent limitations in reasoning over evolving user requirements across turns.

AI.brief_summary: TurnFlow 是面向多轮 LLM 助手的交互式基准，用场景引导的自适应用户模拟配合可验证判分，检验模型能否在对话中保持、修订并真正执行不断变化的用户需求；9 个模型在 490 个场景上的通过率为 42.86%–59.59%，并在 Scope Creep、Goal Shift 上明显更差。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本任务、无视觉 latent，但它把「察觉到约束」与「在最终回答中执行约束」分开检验，并隐藏关键需求由模拟用户展开，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真被答案使用、以及视觉旁路/未执行问题的评测设计借鉴。
